content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain French toast is made from whole‑grain bread soaked in a mixture of eggs, milk, and spices, then fried until golden. It offers a more nutritious alternative to classic French toast, retaining the fiber and micronutrients of whole grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic French toast recipe dates back to 17th‑century France as a way to use stale bread.
Whole‑grain bread contains two to three times more fiber than white bread, aiding digestion.
Adding cinnamon and vanilla to the batter gives the toast a warm, aromatic flavor.
In many countries French toast is served with berries, honey, or maple syrup.
Baking the toast in the oven reduces the amount of added oil.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread provides dietary fiber that supports healthy bowel function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates release energy slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and whole‑grain bread supply B1, B2, B3, and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs add complete protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Cinnamon and vanilla contain polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the eggs used in the batter.

items.title: High sugar when topped
items.content: Maple syrup, honey, or sugary toppings can significantly increase calories and glycemic load.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the whole‑grain bread is salted, total sodium intake should be considered.

items.title: Gluten restrictions
items.content: People on a gluten‑free diet need to choose a gluten‑free whole‑grain bread alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the toast hot, drizzled with maple syrup, honey, or berry sauce, and sprinkle with nuts or dried fruit. It pairs well with yogurt for breakfast or can be used as a base for savory sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep whole‑grain bread in a cool, dry place in an airtight container. Cooked French toast is best consumed within 2–3 days, stored in the refrigerator, and reheated in a toaster or oven before serving.
